title: Built from the roots.
shortDescription: Understanding what happens beneath the abstraction.
html:
The foundation

Programming fundamentals, low-level exploration, and self-directed experimentation form the roots of my engineering work.

My contribution

Working across C, C++, and C# built an understanding of memory, execution, types, and the boundaries between managed and native software.

Evidence

I achieved 98% in the Software Developer & Tester Technician Exam. The projects that follow show how those foundations developed into professional software, infrastructure, and AI systems.

title: Beneath the interface.
shortDescription: Following software all the way down to its runtime.
html:
Context

Reverse engineering was an early route into understanding how compiled software behaves beyond its documented interfaces.

My contribution

I developed a CS:GO internal mod menu with native C++ and ImGui, including custom Radio1/audio functionality. The work involved runtime modification, binary analysis, Windows internals, and hooking concepts.

Engineering focus

The challenge was connecting low-level execution to usable tooling: investigating behavior, reasoning about process state, and debugging native integrations.

What it led to

That work provided a foundation for native integration at FyreZone and a continuing interest in the layers beneath high-level APIs.

title: Across the native boundary.
shortDescription: Connecting native C++ with a higher-level runtime.
html:
Context

My work at FyreZone Kft. applied native development knowledge to integrations around Node.js and anti-cheat-related systems.

My contribution

I worked on C++ development and a native Node.js module, connecting low-level functionality to an application runtime.

Engineering focus

The central concern was the boundary between native implementation and higher-level integration. This entry describes the engineering scope without exposing proprietary implementation details.

title: Built to keep working.
shortDescription: Evolving production software through its difficult edges.
html:
Context

Enterprise software brings existing behavior, legacy code, and production constraints. My work at Griffsoft spans C#/.NET application development and the systems around it.

My contribution

I worked with WinForms, middleware, authentication, Keycloak integration, OAuth/OpenID Connect, and PKCE. Other areas included PDF and Excel functionality, framework migrations, refactoring, code review, and CI/CD.

Difficult engineering work

Resource-management investigations included GDI, font, and memory leaks. Production debugging required tracing behavior across application layers rather than treating symptoms in isolation.

Perspective

This work strengthened the connection between implementation, maintainability, and responsibility for software already in use.

title: The whole system.
shortDescription: Owning the path from client update to server reliability.
html:
Context

Running a Shaiya MMORPG private server brings application development and infrastructure operation into the same system.

My contribution

The work covers the game server, client management, website, backend, database, update and patch infrastructure, deployment, and administration.

Reliability and protection

Networking, IP protection, and DDoS mitigation are part of the operating architecture. The server has repeatedly been targeted by DDoS attacks; so far, the protection architecture has prevented those attempts from causing meaningful disruption.

Engineering focus

The system must remain understandable across boundaries: client distribution, application services, storage, and network protection. Reliability is an ongoing operational responsibility.

title: Knowledge, made local.
shortDescription: Thousands of catalogs. One locally running intelligence system.
html:
The problem

Technical parts information was distributed across 4,500+ PDF catalogs. Making that collection useful required more than placing documents behind a chat interface.

My contribution

The system combines OCR, vision-based extraction, structured processing, and multimodal document handling. Approximately 1.6 million structured part records were extracted from the catalog collection.

Architecture

Documents flow through extraction into SQL storage and a vector index. Hybrid retrieval combines structured constraints with semantic search. A tool-calling AI agent retrieves relevant parts information and PDFs.

Entirely local

The entire AI stack runs locally, including model inference with llama.cpp and GPU acceleration. Deployment work includes concurrent usage and VRAM/RAM optimization on local hardware.

Engineering decisions

The central design task is choosing the right retrieval mechanism for each question: precise structured lookup, semantic retrieval, or a combination. Local deployment makes memory allocation and inference capacity part of the application architecture.

title: Beyond the API call.
shortDescription: Typed contracts for streaming, tools, and agent execution.
html:
Context

CrideLLMApi represents a transition from consuming AI APIs to engineering the infrastructure around them.

My contribution

The abstraction covers OpenAI-compatible chat completions, embeddings, and model endpoints, with strongly typed DTOs and asynchronous generation.

Streaming and execution

SSE streaming, context management, function/tool calling, typed tool arguments, tool execution, and agent loops form the execution layer.

Local providers

Local model providers and llama.cpp integration support experiments with custom agentic execution. The focus is explicit contracts across generation, tool use, and application control flow.

title: Evidence, not just answers.
shortDescription: Engineering traceable retrieval for clinical research.
html:
Research context

My current university thesis explores clinical document retrieval and cohort discovery. The focus here is the engineering architecture, not clinical advice or claims of clinical validation.

System design

Hybrid structured and semantic search supports inclusion and exclusion criteria. Agentic retrieval helps investigate relevant evidence across clinical documents.

Traceability

Evidence verification, traceable results, and audit trails are central system concerns. A result should remain connected to the material that supports it.

Privacy-aware engineering

Local medical language models and document processing are considered within a privacy-aware architecture. This is the newest growth in my work: applying retrieval infrastructure to research-oriented systems.
